'''Rimhak Ree''' ({{Korean|hangul=이임학}}; December 18, 1922 – January 9, 2005), alternatively '''Im-hak Ree''', was a [[Korean Canadians|Korean Canadian]] mathematician. He contributed in the field of [[group theory]], most notably with the concept of the [[Ree group]] in {{harvs|last=Ree|year1=1960|year2=1961}}.

==Early life==
Ree received his early education in [[Hamhung]], [[Kankyōnan-dō]], [[Korea under Japanese rule|Korea, Empire of Japan]] (now in [[North Korea]]). He attended the Hamhung #1 Public Ordinary School ({{lang|ko|함흥 제 1공립보통학교}}), and in 1934 entered the Hamhung Public High School ({{lang|ko|함흥공립고등보통학교}}).<ref>{{harvnb|Ju|2007|p=2}}</ref> He went on to [[Keijō Imperial University]], where he studied physics, which was an unusual choice for Koreans at the time. Ree graduated in 1944 with a physics degree; he then went to Fengtian, [[Manchukuo]] (today [[Shenyang]], [[Liaoning]] in the [[People's Republic of China]]) to work for an aircraft company.

==Career==
After the [[surrender of Japan]] in 1945 and the end of [[Korea under Japanese rule|Japanese rule in Korea]], Ree returned to his hometown of Hamhung and briefly took up a professorship at the invitation of the newly established [[Kim Il-sung University]], but soon escaped to South Korea and was appointed as an assistant professor in the Department of Mathematics at [[Seoul National University]] in early 1947.<ref name = "khan"/> Later that year, in [[Namdaemun Market]], Ree found an issue of the Bulletin of the [[American Mathematical Society]], which proposedly was left by an American soldier. On the Bulletin was the paper 'Note on power series', in which [[Max August Zorn|Max Zorn]] solved a problem about the convergence of certain power series with complex coefficients. In the paper, Zorn posed a question of whether the same result held for power series with real coefficients.<ref name="MacTutor">{{cite web|title=Rimhak Ree|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Ree.html|website=MacTutor History of Mathematics|access-date=3 April 2018}}</ref> Ree solved the problem and sent the solution to Max Zorn. When Zorn received Ree's solution, it was sent to the Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society to be published in 1949 with the title 'On a problem of Max Zorn' and become the first mathematical paper published by a Korean in an international journal.<ref name="MacTutor"/>

At the beginning of the [[Korean War]], he failed to evacuate and remained in North Korean-occupied Seoul, living in hiding to avoid conscription by the [[Korean People's Army]]. He fled south to [[Busan]] in 1951, after the [[Third Battle of Seoul]] took place.<ref name = "khan"/>

In 1953 he was awarded a Canadian scholarship to allow him to study for a Ph.D. degree at the [[University of British Columbia]] in [[Vancouver]], [[Canada]].<ref>{{harvnb|Ju|2007|p=3}}</ref> He completed his dissertation on [[Witt algebra]]s in 1955. His thesis advisor was [[Stephen Arthur Jennings]]. Following the award of his doctorate, Ree was appointed as a lecturer at [[Montana State University]], despite facing several problems regarding his labour permission and nationality.

In mid-1955, Ree received a grant from the National Research Council of Canada and he worked with Jennings on Lie algebras. In 1958, he published a solution to a problem of [[Paul Erdős]] regarding a certain [[class (set theory)|class]] of [[irrational numbers]].<ref>{{cite journal| last=Ree |first=Rimhak |title=4773: A class of irrational numbers. Proposed by Paul Erdős. |journal=[[The American Mathematical Monthly]] |volume=65 |issue=10 |page=782 |doi=10.2307/2310698|jstor=2310698 }} The following year he also co-authored a paper with Michael Marcus, who had an [[Erdős number]] of two via [[Ralph P. Boas Jr.]] {{cite journal| last1=Marcus |first1=M. |last2=Ree|first2=R |title=Diagonals of doubly stochastic matrices |journal=The Quarterly Journal of Mathematics |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=296–302 |year=1959 |doi=10.1093/qmath/10.1.296}}</ref> Ree's two most renowned papers were written from 1960 to 1961, in which he suggested a Lie type group over a finite field [[Ree group|now named after him]]. In 1962 after being promoted to an assistant professor in mathematics at University of British Columbia, he was granted an academic year which he spent in [[Yale University|Yale]]. He was elected a member of [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 1964.

==Personal life==
Ree had two daughters Erran and Hiran from his first marriage.<ref name="VancouverSun2005">{{cite news |url=https://vancouversunandprovince.remembering.ca/obituary/rimhak-ree-1065819045 |title=Rimhak Ree, December 18, 1922 – January 9, 2005 |newspaper=[[Vancouver Sun]] |date=12 January 2005 |access-date=27 June 2022}}</ref> He later married Rhoda Mah, a doctor and the daughter of John Ming Mah, who owned  Northwest Food Products, a manufacturers of noodles. She would go on to work as staff physician for [[Canadian Pacific Airlines]]. Rimhak and Rhoda's first son Ronald was followed by another son Robert in December 1971.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=m8krAQAAIAAJ&q=%22rhoda+ree%22 |title=Season's Greetings | newspaper=Chinatown News |volume=18 |issue=2 |year=1971 |page=56}}</ref> They also had a third son Richard.<ref name="VancouverSun2005"/>

Around the time Ree received his doctorate, [[Republic of Korea passport|his passport]] was approaching its expiration date, so he visited the {{ill|Consulate General of South Korea, San Francisco|ko|주샌프란시스코 대한민국 총영사관|lt=South Korean consulate in San Francisco}} to extend it, but instead the consular officer ordered him to return to South Korea.<ref name="JuEtAl1996">{{cite journal |url=https://koreascience.kr/article/JAKO199659334994069.pdf |last1=Ju |first1=Jin-gu |author-mask=주진구 [Ju Jin-gu]; |last2=Gwon |first2=Gyeong-hwan |author2-mask=권경환 [Gwon Gyeong-hwan]; |last3=Go |first3=Yeong-so |author3-mask=고영소 [Go Yeong-so]; |last4=Yi |first4=Jeong-rim |author4-mask=이정림 [Yi Jeong-rim] |title=원로와의 대담: 세계적 수학권위자 李林學 박사 |trans-title=Conversations with doyens: world-renowned mathematics authority Dr. Ree Rimhak |script-journal=ko:과학과 기술 |trans-journal=Science & Technology |publisher=Korean Federation of Science and Technology Societies |volume=29 |issue=12 |pages=80–82 |year=1996 |issn=1599-7340 }}</ref><ref name="Hankyoreh1997">{{cite news |url=https://newslibrary.naver.com/viewer/index.naver?articleId=1997061100289113001&editNo=5&printCount=1&publishDate=1997-06-11&officeId=00028&pageNo=13&printNo=2902&publishType=00010 |last=Sin |first=Dong-ho |author-mask=신동호 [Sin Dong-ho] |title=두종류의'단순군'찾아내 최고 수학자 세계적 영예 |newspaper=[[The Hankyoreh]] |date=11 June 1997 |page=13 |access-date=27 June 2022 |via=Naver News Library}}</ref> As he refused and his passport was revoked, Ree became ''de facto'' [[statelessness|stateless]]. He later received [[permanent residency in Canada]] and continued to work at the University of British Columbia.<ref name="JuEtAl1996"/><ref name="MacTutor"/>

Ree's family was [[divided family|divided]] by the Korean War, with his father, older sister, and other relatives having stayed in their hometown of Hamhung. He reportedly visited North Korea using his [[Canadian passport]] various times for academic exchanges, but he was not able to travel freely in North Korea and thus had no success in making contact with his relatives. Ree requested help from Erdős, who as an internationally-famous Hungarian citizen faced fewer restrictions on travel or communication in either capitalist or communist countries. In the 1980s, Erdős was able to make contact with several relatives of Ree's with the help of Hungary's [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Hungary)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] and the country's embassy in Pyongyang, and sent Ree an envelope containing their letters, photographs, and addresses. Ree forwarded the envelope to his mother and younger sister in South Korea, which reportedly resulted in them being investigated by [[Korean Central Intelligence Agency|South Korea's intelligence services]].<ref name = "khan"/> Furthermore, his visits to North Korea led South Korea's [[Park Chung Hee]] government to place an entry ban on him. His entry ban was lifted in 1996, when he was invited to the 50th anniversary ceremony of the [[Korean Mathematical Society]].<ref name = "khan">{{cite news |url=https://www.khan.co.kr/national/national-general/article/201510302151325 |last=Bak |first=Eun-ha |author-mask=박은하 [Bak Eun-ha] |title=세계적 천재 수학자 이임학을 기억하는 국가의 방식 |newspaper=[[Kyunghyang Shinmun]] |date=30 October 2015 |access-date=30 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.hankyung.com/news/article/2016052217251 |last=Bak |first=Geun-tae |author-mask=박근태 [Bak Geun-tae] |title=국가가 버린 세계적 수학자 이임학, '리군이론'으로 수학사에 족적 |newspaper=[[Korea Economic Daily]] |page=A19 |date=21 May 2016 |access-date=27 June 2022}}</ref>

He suffered from [[Alzheimer's disease]] in his later years.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.chosun.com/opinion/specialist_column/2024/03/20/4JETIAPMWNGPBDZAVQ2ZUZRL7I/ |last=Min |first=Tae-gi |title=한국 최초 국제 학술 논문 주인공… 갈루아와 나란히 '최고 수학자' 반열에 |newspaper=[[Chosun Ilbo]] |date=22 March 2024 |access-date=7 June 2026}}</ref> Ree died on January 9, 2005, in [[Vancouver]], Canada.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.koreascience.kr/article/JAKO200556605505042.page |last=Ju |first=Jin-gu |author-mask=주진구 [Ju Jin-gu] |title=선구적 수학자 이임학(李林學)선생을 추모하며 |journal=The Science & Technology |trans-title=In memory of pioneering mathematician Ree Rimhak |script-journal=ko:과학과 기술 |trans-journal=Science & Technology |publisher=Korean Federation of Science and Technology Societies |volume=38 |issue=2 |year=2005 |pages=21 |issn=1599-7340 }}</ref>
